In sum, the decision to hold oral hearings, whether in Washington, by region, or by joint boards is one solely within the discretion of this Commission, and, absent a showing that such discretion has been abused, there is no basis for requiring that any type of oral hearing be held.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS
This rulemaking has been initiated to reexamine the exemptions from Federal economic regulation embodied in sections 203(b)(8) and 202(c) of the Interstate Commerce Act. Our immediate focus is on discerning the proper geographic limits of the "zone adjacent to and commercially a part of" a base municipality. The present population-mileage formula defining the commercial zone exemption was prescribed in the mid-1940's. Since that time there has been an enormous increase in our nation's population with an increasing share of this population residing in urban areas. 11 As noted in the Interim Report, concurrently with the growth in city size, technological and social developments have caused concomitant changes in the structure of urban area environments,
We note that the trend of an ever-increasing population shift to the city seems to be subsiding. Bureau of Census figures indicate that the non-metropolitan growth rate between 1970 and 1974 was 5.6 percent, as compared to the 3.4 percent growth rate in metropolitan areas. This is the first period in our history, except during the Great Depression of the 1930's, that the metropolitan growth rate has been lower.
